text:
**Findings**
High: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:110) lines 110-163 accepts negative `AllocCPUS` and GPU counts, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.

High: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:70) lines 70-84 lets older terminal records overwrite newer terminal records because all terminal states share rank `2`.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:74) lines 74-80 marks rows unchanged when only `state`, `end`, and `elapsed_sec` match, silently ignoring changed user/partition/resource/exit-code fields.

Medium: [jobwatch/parser.py](/work/jobwatch/parser.py:118) lines 118-126 and [jobwatch/reports.py](/work/jobwatch/reports.py:14) lines 14-65 allow timezone-bearing ISO strings but compare timestamps lexicographically in SQLite, which can filter records incorrectly across offsets.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) lines 13-26 defines no `CHECK` constraints, so malformed negative resources or empty identity fields can persist if inserted outside the parser.

Medium: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:52) lines 52-58 and [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:121) lines 121-180 make report commands create a brand-new empty database for a typo path instead of failing.

Medium: [jobwatch/cli.py](/work/jobwatch/cli.py:90) lines 90-180 does not catch SQLite errors, so corrupt DBs, locked DBs, and invalid DB paths can produce raw tracebacks.

Low: [jobwatch/db.py](/work/jobwatch/db.py:13) lines 13-26 has no indexes for report filters/orderings, so every report scans the full `jobs` table as data grows.

Low: [pyproject.toml](/work/pyproject.toml:7) line 7 and [jobwatch/__init__.py](/work/jobwatch/__init__.py:3) line 3 duplicate the package version, creating release drift risk.

Overall quality score: **6/10**. The project is small, readable, and has a useful test suite (`61 passed`), but I would not approve it as-is because the data-integrity bugs can produce wrong accounting reports.

Estimated rewrite/significant-change size: **110 lines**, mostly validation, schema constraints/indexes, upsert freshness logic, DB-open behavior, error handling, and targeted tests.

Bottom line: **No, I would not approve this as-is.**

issues.description: Negative AllocCPUS and GPU counts are accepted, allowing negative CPU/GPU-hour reports.
Older terminal records can overwrite newer terminal records because all terminal states share the same rank.
Rows are treated as unchanged using only state, end, and elapsed_sec, so changed resource or exit-code fields are ignored.
Timezone-bearing ISO timestamps are compared lexicographically, which can produce incorrect since-window filtering.
The schema has no CHECK constraints to protect against invalid resources or empty identity fields.
Report commands create an empty database for a missing DB path instead of reporting a likely typo.
SQLite operational errors are not handled, so corrupt or locked databases can surface raw tracebacks.
No indexes support report filters or ordering, forcing full-table scans as the jobs table grows.
Package version is duplicated with jobwatch/__init__.py, creating release drift risk.
